我做 A 股量化，先学会了怎么不骗自己 本来想少追新闻、多按规则做事，结果先和行情、财报版本、回测假设较上了劲。从 B／B＋到 ATR 和动量，这篇把做过的实验与踩过的坑一起翻出来。 最开始想做 A 股量化，念头很朴素：少一点追着新闻跑，少一点盘中一激动就改主意，把选股、买卖和风控写成能反复检查的规则。听起来像是给交易装个自动驾驶，真正做起来才发现，第一件事居然是先检查油表是不是坏的😅。

这篇写的是我和 Claude、Codex 一起做的策略研究、数据排错和虚拟回测。里面的收益都是研究组合的历史模拟结果，不是我的实盘收益。一路折腾下来，我花在“这串数字到底靠不靠谱”上的时间，比挑选一个听起来很厉害的指标多得多。

**先把“看着不错”翻译成规则。** 我们先整理原来的想法，再把偏短的波段方案 A 和偏中期的方案 B 放在同一套约束下比较。不能一个版本满仓、另一个大部分时间空仓，最后只看谁回撤小就宣布胜利；暂停以后一直等着，还是假设过一段时间恢复，结果也可能差很多。

后来重点研究的 B，可以理解为“先过质量筛选，再等趋势信号”。下面这些是当时冻结的实验参数，方便看懂我们到底在测什么，不是让我今天看到一只符合条件的股票就立刻冲进去：

1. 先限定沪深主板普通 A 股，至少有 250 个有效上市交易日；历史 ST、退市整理、停牌和状态不明的股票需要按当时情况处理。
2. 最近三个已公布年度的归母净利润加权平均 ROE 都不低于 10%，最近年报每股经营现金流为正，资产负债率不超过 70%；近 20 个有效交易日日均成交额不少于 5000 万元。
3. 大盘这一关，用最近完成交易日的沪深 300 收盘与其 60 日简单均线比较。严格高于才考虑新开仓，缺数据也不能默认放行。
4. 个股收盘严格突破此前 60 个有效交易日的最高收盘，同时高于 120 日均线；当日量不低于此前 20 日均量，真实涨幅低于 7%。突破窗口和均量窗口都不把当天塞进去凑数。
5. 当天收盘才能确认的信号，留到下一交易日考虑。还要核对交易状态、参考价和实际可执行报价，不能看完开盘价，再假装自己提前按这个价买到了。

规则写下来以后，很多原本觉得“差不多”的地方就躲不过去了。突破是大于，还是大于等于？均线包不包含当天？没有指数数据时，是停止还是继续？这些小符号真能改变后面的交易，不是文案里的标点。

**买多少，往往比选中谁更难。** B 的实验里，单笔名义风险预算是权益的 0.4%，配 10% 的名义止损，算出来大约是 4% 的单股目标仓位，还要同时受单股 6% 上限、同行业 15% 上限和最多 6 只的限制。再看现金、费用和手数，不够一手就放弃，不能为了让程序“买成功”硬把仓位抬上去。

出场条件也写死：收盘相对经公司行为调整的买入成本跌 10% 或更多、跌破 60 日均线，或者持有满 120 个有效交易日，就在下一交易日提出退出候选。这里最容易自我安慰的是那个“10%”：写了止损，不等于市场承诺只让我亏 10%。跳空、停牌、跌停和无法成交，都可能让实际结果更难看。

账户层面还有一条高水位回撤 10% 暂停新开仓的规则。它不是自动清仓，更不是最大亏损保险。至少经过 20 个完整交易日复盘，再决定是否恢复。历史实验里有一类情景是假设每次暂停后都获准恢复，这只是为了比较规则的假设，不能拿来冒充现实里已经批准的操作。

**数据下载完了，离“数据能用”还差一大截。** 第一轮排查拿到 3378 份原始行情文件，结构检查后有 3328 份通过，50 份隔离；另外还有 6 个代码没有下载到行情，单独列着。那 50 份里有非正价格等问题，我们没有把负数改成零，也没有拿别的证券代码补个空位，让回测看起来终于能跑。

程序这边补了几道检查：列名、日期顺序和重复日期，价格是否有限且为正，高低价关系是否合理，成交量和成交额是否有效。坏缓存要明确报错；新下载先写临时文件，再读回来检查，通过后才替换正式文件。每轮输入还留来源、范围和文件哈希，免得昨天跑的和今天跑的其实已经不是同一批东西。

但结构过关只是“表格没明显散架”。成交量单位、复权、财报版本、历史证券资格，照样能把结果带跑偏。我们找到过一条已知数据实现按股票代码前缀处理成交量的路径；交叉检查的 3 只证券、8 个证券日样本里，两边成交量接近差 100 倍。处理方式是阻断那条已确认有问题的来源路径，再尝试下一来源，旧文件先保留。不能因为查出几个样本，就把所有缓存统统乘 100，宣布全市场修复完成。

**财报的“年份”，也不等于当时已经知道。** 这是我后来越查越头大的地方。今天接口里显示的某年财报，可能已经更正或重述；某个公告日期字段，也未必就是数字第一次公开的日子。把今天能查到的版本直接塞回过去，相当于让过去的自己偷看了一眼答案。

我们做过同一报告期不同版本的对照，也查过资产、负债和权益能不能对上。有些差异确实存在，但发现差异不等于已经证明某笔交易会改变：还得看首次披露时间、有没有跨策略阈值，以及那时是否满足其余条件。所以这部分没有“全修好了”的漂亮结尾，原始数据、候选版本和核查报告都留着，继续往下查。

**B＋：把 60 日突破改成 40 日，会不会更早上车？** 这个想法很自然，所以我们只改了这一项，其他主要规则保持一致，做 B60 和 B＋40 的对照。11 月 2 日那轮的三个历史区间，放宽后只改善了一个；最近区间反而从约 -3.67% 变成 -4.17%。把佣金和滑点抬高后，B＋也没有变好看。

这轮没有给出“升级就能更赚钱”的证据。后来获准做的是两套虚拟账本的前瞻影子观察，不是让 B＋接管账户。观察至少 20 个完整交易日，也是检查流程和记录的方法，天数到了不会自动解锁“稳定盈利”成就。

**再加 ATR 和动量，结果也没顺着愿望走。** 11 月 6 日我们把基线 B、只改 ATR 仓位、只改波动调整动量排序拆开测试，三个历史区间，加上最近区间的高成本情景，共 12 组。两项没有混在一起，免得最后连是谁起作用都说不清。

ATR 版本试着让波动大的股票少买一点；动量版本则把 60 日涨幅除以相应的波动尺度，在同一批候选里重新排顺序。指标库还实现了 38 个价格、成交类指标；没有可靠数据的财报、估值或盘口项目，就留空并标记缺失，不拿一个默认零把它糊过去。

这一轮最近的标准情景，区间是 2023 年 1 月 3 日至 2026 年 10 月 27 日，各组分别从 10 万元虚拟资金开始。下面是整段总收益和最大回撤，不是年化：

- 基线 B：总收益约 -3.69%，最大回撤约 -11.19%。
- 只改 ATR 仓位：总收益约 -4.31%，最大回撤约 -11.36%。
- 只改波动调整动量排序：总收益约 +5.50%，最大回撤约 -9.19%。

高成本情景下，动量版总收益降到约 +1.89%。它通过了事先设定的进一步研究筛查，ATR 版没有通过。但动量版在 2019—2022 年的回撤反而更大，最近区间平均仓位也比基线高。把收益拆到年份、再对已有日收益做区块重采样后，差异估计仍跨过零。看到一个正数就准备开香槟的话，后面这几页报告大概就是负责拔塞子的手。

而且这些历史已经被我们看过了，不能改完参数再假装它们是全新的考试题。回测仍有财报时点、历史资格、复权成交代理价等限制。这个 +5.50% 值得继续查，不够拿来给未来收益打包票。

**一轮实验，我到底留下什么。** 我现在更在意能不能复查整个过程：先冻结输入和参数，再生成候选、虚拟成交、现金与每日净值；跑完把 CSV 重新读回来，用独立计算核对收益、回撤和现金，而不是让同一个函数给自己盖章。

项目里也留了复现入口。比如 B／B＋对照这一轮，需要本机已有的日线、财报和指数数据，指定一个尚不存在的新输出目录；它是项目内的研究脚本，不是下载这一段命令就能直接交易的软件：

```powershell
python research/compare_bplus_20261102.py --data-root "自己的历史数据目录" --output "新的研究输出目录"
python research/test_bplus_signal_20261102.py
python research/test_bplus_shadow.py
```

新参数那轮还把 11139 条每日净值重新构建了一遍。历史印花税也改成分日期处理，不能拿今天的成本一路套回过去；2023 年 8 月 28 日起减半征收的时间点，对照的是 [财政部、税务总局公告](https://www.mof.gov.cn/jrttts/202308/t20230828_3904235.htm)。这些检查能发现实现错误，但没办法替不可靠的历史数据洗白。

为了把不同轮次分清楚，我另外放了一份 [公开研究摘要](https://young7788-web.github.io/assets/research/a-share-quant-study-summary.json)，列出本次文章引用的参数实验、区间、虚拟资金和限制。真实持仓、账户资料和访问凭据不放在公开文章里。

**折腾到现在，我真正改掉了一点什么。** 我还没研究出一台按按钮就吐钱的机器，倒是越来越不敢随口说“这个策略稳”。信号多一点不等于更好，少交易也不自动等于风控优秀；回测能跑、数字能复算、数据真的可用、现实里能成交，是几道不同的关。

眼下我继续做数据核对和规则观察，新研究不会自动覆盖原来的执行规则，具体操作也另行确认。以前我更着急问“能赚多少”，现在会先问一句：这个结果，有没有可能只是程序很认真地算错了？这句不怎么热血，但能让我少上几次自己的当。

Building my A-share quant research process A first-person account of strategy rules, data audits and simulated backtests. I started looking into A-share quant trading for a simple reason. I wanted to spend less time chasing headlines or changing my mind in the middle of a session and put stock selection, entries, exits and risk controls into rules I could check repeatedly. It sounded like putting trading on autopilot. The first thing I actually had to do was check whether the fuel gauge was broken 😅.

This is about strategy research, data troubleshooting and simulated backtests I did with Claude and Codex. The returns are historical simulations of research portfolios. They aren't returns from my own live account. I spent much more time asking whether a number was reliable than picking indicators that sounded impressive.

**Turning “looks good” into rules.** We organized the original ideas and compared the shorter swing strategy A with the medium-term strategy B under the same constraints. It wouldn't make sense to keep one fully invested and the other mostly in cash, then just declare the one with the smaller drawdown the winner. What you assume after a pause matters, too: staying out indefinitely and allowing trading to resume can produce very different results.

We focused on B, which screened for quality and then waited for a trend signal. These were the parameters frozen for the experiment. They're here to show exactly what we tested.

1. Start with ordinary A shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen main boards that have at least 250 valid trading days since listing. Handle historical ST designations, delisting periods, suspensions and unknown status as they stood at the time.
2. Require weighted-average ROE based on net income attributable to shareholders of the parent of at least 10% in each of the last three published annual reports. The latest annual report must show positive operating cash flow per share and a debt-to-assets ratio no higher than 70%. Average daily turnover over the last 20 valid sessions must be at least 50 million yuan.
3. For the market filter, compare the CSI 300 close from the last completed session with its 60-day simple moving average. Consider new positions only when the close is strictly above it. Missing data doesn't pass the filter.
4. The stock must close strictly above the highest close of the previous 60 valid sessions and above its 120-day moving average. Volume must be at least the previous 20-day average, and the actual gain must be under 7%. Neither lookback window includes the current session.
5. A signal confirmed at the close can only be considered the next trading day. Check trading status, the reference price and an executable quote. You can't look at the opening price and pretend you bought at it in advance.

Writing down the rules forced us to answer questions we'd been able to gloss over. Is a breakout strictly greater than the threshold, or can it equal it? Does the moving average include today? Do we stop or keep going if index data is missing? Those small differences change trades.

**Deciding how much to buy can be harder than picking what to buy.** B used a nominal risk budget of 0.4% of equity per trade and a nominal stop of 10%, implying a target position of roughly 4%. The caps were 6% per stock, 15% per industry and six holdings. Cash, fees and lot sizes also applied. If the budget couldn't buy one lot, we skipped the trade.

The exit rules were fixed too. A close 10% or more below the corporate-action-adjusted purchase cost, a close below the 60-day moving average, or a holding period of 120 valid trading days generated an exit candidate for the next session. A 10% stop sets a rule for generating a signal. Gaps, suspensions, limit-down moves and failed fills can make the actual loss worse.

At portfolio level, a 10% drawdown from the high-water mark paused new entries. It did not liquidate positions or cap losses. We would review after at least 20 full trading days before deciding whether to resume. One backtest scenario assumed that each pause ended with permission to resume. That was an assumption for comparing rules, separate from any actual authorization.

**Downloading data is a long way from having usable data.** The first audit found 3,378 raw market files. Of those, 3,328 passed structural checks and 50 were quarantined. Another six tickers had no downloaded data and were listed separately. Some quarantined files contained nonpositive prices. We didn't turn negatives into zeros or fill holes with another security's data to make the test run.

We added checks for columns, date order and duplicates, finite positive prices, reasonable high and low prices, and valid volume and turnover. A bad cache should produce a clear error. New downloads go to a temporary file, get read back and validated, and only then replace the live file. Each run records the input sources, scope and hashes so we can tell whether two runs used the same data.

Passing structural checks only tells us the table hasn't obviously fallen apart. Volume units, price adjustments, filing revisions and historical eligibility can still skew results. We identified a data implementation that handled volumes by ticker prefix. A cross-check of three securities across eight security-days found volume figures nearly 100 times apart. We blocked that confirmed problem path, tried the next source and kept the old files. A handful of samples didn't justify multiplying every cached volume by 100.

**A financial statement's year doesn't tell you when it was known.** A report available from an API today may have been corrected or restated. A date field may not be the day its figures first became public. Using today's version in the past gives the simulated trader a peek at the answer.

We compared versions for the same reporting period and checked whether assets, liabilities and equity reconciled. Some differences were real. To show that any one trade changed, we would still need the first disclosure date, whether the difference crossed a strategy threshold, and whether the other conditions were met. We kept the raw data, candidate versions and audit reports for further investigation.

**B+: would a 40-day breakout get us in earlier than a 60-day breakout?** We changed just the breakout window and compared B60 with B+40. In the November 2 run, the looser rule improved only one of three historical windows. The most recent window went from around -3.67% to -4.17%. Higher commissions and slippage did not improve the case for B+.

That test didn't establish that the change would make more money. What was approved afterward was forward shadow observation using two virtual ledgers. At least 20 full trading days gives us time to check the process and records. It doesn't unlock an achievement called “consistently profitable.”

**ATR and momentum didn't give me quite the results I wanted either.** On November 6 we tested baseline B, sizing changed to use ATR alone, and volatility-adjusted momentum ranking alone. Three historical windows plus a high-cost scenario in the most recent window made 12 combinations. Changing the two features separately let us tell what each did.

The ATR version tried buying less of more volatile stocks. The momentum version divided the 60-day gain by a volatility measure and reordered the same candidates. The indicator library also implemented 38 price and volume indicators. We marked financial, valuation and order-book fields as missing when reliable data wasn't available.

The latest standard scenario ran from January 3, 2023 through October 27, 2026. Each run started with 100,000 yuan in simulated capital. These are total returns for that period and maximum drawdowns, without annualizing returns.

- Baseline B: total return about -3.69%, maximum drawdown about -11.19%.
- ATR sizing only: total return about -4.31%, maximum drawdown about -11.36%.
- Volatility-adjusted momentum ranking only: total return about +5.50%, maximum drawdown about -9.19%.

Under higher costs, momentum's total return dropped to about +1.89%. It passed a research screen set in advance and ATR didn't. Momentum did have a worse drawdown in 2019–2022 and a higher average allocation than baseline in the latest window. After breaking down returns by year and block-resampling the observed daily returns, the estimated difference still crossed zero. If a positive number made me reach for the champagne, the rest of that report made me put it back.

We've already seen this historical data. Changing a parameter doesn't turn it into a new exam. The results still have limits around the timing of financial statements, historical eligibility and adjusted execution-price proxies. The +5.50% is worth following up on and is no guarantee of future returns.

**What I keep after a run.** I care more now about being able to review the whole process. Freeze the inputs and parameters, generate candidates, simulated fills, cash and daily equity, then read back the CSV files and calculate return, drawdown and cash independently. I don't want a function signing off on its own work.

The project includes reproduction commands. The B/B+ comparison requires local daily bars, financial statements and index data, with a new output directory that doesn't already exist. These are research scripts from the project, not standalone trading software.

```powershell
python research/compare_bplus_20261102.py --data-root "YOUR_HISTORICAL_DATA_DIRECTORY" --output "NEW_RESEARCH_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY"
python research/test_bplus_signal_20261102.py
python research/test_bplus_shadow.py
```

For the newer parameter run we also reconstructed 11,139 daily equity records. We handled historical stamp duty by date instead of applying today's costs all the way back. For the reduction by half starting August 28, 2023, we used the [announcement from the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration](https://www.mof.gov.cn/jrttts/202308/t20230828_3904235.htm). These checks can catch implementation errors. They can't rescue unreliable source data.

I put the tested parameter sets, periods, simulated capital and limitations into a [public research summary](https://young7788-web.github.io/assets/research/a-share-quant-study-summary.json) to keep the runs straight. My actual holdings, account records and credentials stay private.

**What has changed for me.** I haven't built a money machine. I'm much more hesitant to say a strategy is reliable. More signals don't automatically help, and fewer trades don't automatically mean better risk management. A runnable backtest, reproducible arithmetic, usable data and executable trades are different hurdles.

I'm still checking data and observing the rules. New research doesn't automatically replace the existing execution rules, and any live action needs separate confirmation. I used to ask, “How much can it make?” Now I'm more likely to ask whether the program could be very diligently calculating the wrong answer. It isn't as exciting, but it helps me fool myself a little less.

我为什么弄这个小站 我学的是电气工程及其自动化，但如果只用“工科生”三个字介绍自己，好像也太省事了。我的电脑里有电路题、半成品网页、视频工程、服务器笔记，手机里还有一些跑完步随手发的碎碎念。 我学的是电气工程及其自动化，但如果只用“工科生”三个字介绍自己，好像也太省事了。我的电脑里有电路题、半成品网页、视频工程、服务器笔记，手机里还有一些跑完步随手发的碎碎念。东西越攒越多，我想给它们找个能长期放着、还能慢慢长大的地方，于是有了这座“数字花园”。

它不是简历，也不准备假装我什么都会。有些东西我确实做成了，有些只做到一半，还有些折腾了好久，最后发现问题根本不在我以为的地方。把这些过程写下来，比只摆一个漂亮成品更有意思。至少下次再踩坑，我可以翻回来看看自己上次是怎么从坑里爬出来的。

这个网站本身就是第一篇作业：先用 GitHub Pages 免费上线，再拿手机关掉代理实测。第一次截图里，卡片一大片空白，我还以为是网络没加载完；后来发现栏目里本来就没文章，固定高度把“没内容”放大成了“坏了”。这次把文章认真补上，页面也跟着重新排。手机能直连是我亲自测到的一次结果，不代表全国每条线路都一样稳。

Why this digital garden A growing place for study, making and everyday notes. I study electrical engineering and automation, but calling myself an engineering student feels like taking the easy way out. My computer is full of circuit problems, half-built websites, video projects and server notes. My phone has stray thoughts I posted after runs. As the pile grew, I wanted somewhere to keep it for the long haul and let it grow. That's how this digital garden started.

It isn't a résumé, and I'm not pretending I can do everything. Some things worked, some got halfway, and some took ages before I found that the problem was somewhere else entirely. Writing down how that happened is more interesting than displaying a polished result. The next time I fall into a hole, I can at least look up how I climbed out last time.

The site itself was my first assignment. I put it on GitHub Pages for free, then turned off the proxy on my phone and tried opening it. The first screenshot had huge blank cards, and I assumed the network was still loading. It turned out the sections didn't have articles yet, and the fixed heights made missing content look like a broken page. This time I filled out the articles and rebuilt the layout around them. A direct connection worked once on my phone. That tells me how that test went, not how every network in China behaves.

有一阵我把学车、家教、背单词、刷题和运动塞进同一天，忙得要命，没学够又会有罪恶感。现在回头看，没必要把那时的每句牢骚都上升成“人生哲学”。我就是累了，会吐槽，也会第二天继续。比起把自己写成永远自律的人，我更愿意承认：我也经常算错题、跑不动，偶尔就是想喝口无糖百事，看看天。

text_en:
Notes from my public posts Study, running, music and everyday scenes recur in an accessible sample of public posts. I've posted quite a few “well, that was today” moments on X. The sky at half past eight, the night after studying, complaints that my runs were getting slower, rainbows, cats, City Pop, and the minor meltdown of getting integration by parts wrong twice. They're short on their own, but together they read like a diary in the wrong order. I'm trying to keep up with study and exercise, and a song, a film or a patch of sky can still stop me in my tracks.

For a while I packed driving lessons, tutoring, vocabulary drills, problem sets and exercise into the same day. I was exhausted and still felt guilty when I hadn't studied enough. Looking back, I don't need to turn every complaint from that period into a philosophy. I was tired, I grumbled, and I carried on the next day. I'd rather admit that I get problems wrong, struggle through runs, and sometimes just want a sugar-free Pepsi and a look at the sky.

I once told the people who follow me to take care of themselves and keep a little hope for the future. That still feels sincere. Having worries doesn't mean worries are all there is. These notes draw on original public posts I can still read. I don't use replies, deleted material or inaccessible old posts to sum up my personality.

我不想把“正在学”包装成“精通”。做这座网站，是想给自己的学习留一份真实进度：一道题怎么想通，一个软件怎么装上，一个项目怎么卡住、改掉、终于跑起来。会的就写清楚，不会的也没必要端着。

现在对我最有用的办法，是把“大方向”拆小：这周把哪道题真的弄懂了，哪个电路图能自己画出来，哪个软件离开教程也会用了。进度慢一点，也比一直在脑子里想“我将来要成为什么人”实在。基本功得补上，项目和职业选择也得落到具体行动上。

我在网上记录这些，也算给自己留一条时间线。以后翻回来，希望能看见自己从“好像懂了”走到“能解释、能动手、能发现哪里还不会”。
text_en:
What I am learning now I study electrical engineering at an undergraduate university in northern China. I'm studying electrical engineering and automation at an undergraduate university in northern China. It's one name on paper, but there's plenty to chew on: mathematics, circuits, control, and turning what I learn in a textbook into something I can use. I'm still working out where I want to go.

I don't want to dress up “learning” as “expertise.” I built this site to keep an honest record of progress: how a problem clicked, how I got a piece of software installed, and where a project got stuck before I changed something and finally made it work. I can explain what I know and be honest about what I don't.

What helps most now is breaking the big questions into smaller ones. What problem did I actually understand this week? What circuit can I draw myself? What software can I use without a tutorial? Slower progress feels more real than imagining who I might one day become. I need to build the fundamentals and turn projects and career choices into concrete steps.

Writing this down gives me a timeline to look back on. I hope it shows a move from “I think I get it” to “I can explain it, do it, and see what I still don't understand.”

聊了一晚上钱和未来，最后发现最该管的是我的注意力 从 BTC 聊到工作、买房和未来，聊完我没找到财富密码，倒是发现自己的注意力该先救一救了。 昨天晚上和一位 teacher 聊了很久，从 BTC 聊到 A 股、美股，又一路聊到工作、买房和结婚。原以为能听点财富密码，结果先被泼了盆冷水：别碰杠杆，也别老想着靠比特币一夜翻身。他尤其看衰 BTC，理由之一是担心量子计算将来会攻破它。这事我现在还没研究明白，先记下这个分歧；不过“越想一夜暴富，越容易一夜暴负”，我倒是越想越觉得扎心。认知外的钱，真不一定轮得到我挣😅。

他的建议是先攒钱，再考虑长期定投美股，最好先攒够 30 万。我听完就想：老师，您这门课的前置条件是不是有点高？对已经有积累的人来说，这是起点；对还在攒第一桶金的人来说，光走到起点就要喘半天。

聊到工作，老中味也慢慢上来了：还是得老老实实上班。他说起身边高校毕业、在腾讯干了十几年也会被裁的人，也说起在机器人企业忙得脚不沾地的同学。我听着反而更拧巴了——一边说工作要稳，一边又是十几年说裁就裁的故事，那个“稳”到底稳在哪儿？

当然，我也知道人总得先养活自己。但有些建议听起来轻飘飘，是因为说话的人和听话的人，脚底下垫的东西不一样。有时候分水岭还真像羊水：别人能从容试错，我先得算这次摔倒要花多少钱。第一桶金难攒，房、车、婚姻又都排着队等钱，几个选择做下去，未来很多年的现金流可能就先安排上了。

所以“30 岁之前先不急着结婚、不买房、不买车”，这套说法我目前是认同的。不是说谁照做就能发财，我只是觉得，自己还没想清楚的长期承诺，没必要因为年龄到了就赶着签。尤其婚姻，投入的钱、时间和感情都很重，哪是办个喜宴就算通关。股票跌了还能关掉行情软件，日子可没这个按钮。

想来想去，我还是想多研究研究量化交易。倒也不是觉得“交易员永远不会被替代”，而是我想真正弄懂一套能反复检验的方法，少一点被新闻标题牵着走。可现实很喜剧：嘴上说要学习，手上还在刷新 X；本来想看一会儿书，三分钟后人已经泡在评论区了。新闻、行情、社交媒体把注意力切得稀碎，最后一天过去，像忙了很多，又说不出到底做成了什么。

这场夜聊之后，我最想先改的居然不是投资组合，而是把自己的注意力拿回来。把手机放远一点，课认真学，身体继续练，AI 和交易慢慢研究。“薄肌＋孙学＋美股＋AI”喊着挺像版本答案，真落到我身上，第一步居然只是：先别刷了，把今天这点事干完😂。
text_en:
A late-night talk about money, the future and my attention A conversation about investing, work and the cost of letting my phone set my priorities. I spent a long time talking with a teacher last night. We went from BTC to Chinese and US stocks, then on to work, buying a home and getting married. I thought I might hear the secret to getting rich. Instead I got a cold shower: stay away from leverage, and don't expect Bitcoin to turn your life around overnight. He's particularly bearish on BTC, partly because he worries future quantum computers could break it. I haven't looked into that enough to take a side. But the harder I chase overnight riches, the easier it is to go broke overnight. That one stung. Money I don't understand probably isn't mine to make 😅.

His advice was to save first and then consider investing a fixed amount regularly in US stocks for the long term. Ideally, start with 300,000 yuan. I thought, “Teacher, aren't the prerequisites for this class a little steep?” For someone with savings, that's the starting line. For someone trying to build their first nest egg, just reaching it takes a lot of breath.

When we got to careers, the familiar Chinese advice came out: get a steady job and work hard. He mentioned graduates who spent more than a decade at Tencent and still got laid off, and classmates at robotics companies who barely had time to sit down. I felt more conflicted. If a job can vanish after ten years, what exactly makes it steady?

I know I have to support myself. Some advice sounds effortless because the person giving it stands on a different footing from the person taking it. Sometimes the divide really is the circumstances you're born into. Someone else can afford to experiment, while I have to calculate what the next fall will cost me. The first nest egg is hard to build, and a home, a car and marriage are all waiting for it. A few decisions can commit years of future cash flow.

For now I'm sympathetic to the idea of not rushing into marriage, a home or a car before 30. Following that rule isn't a route to riches. I just don't want to sign up for long commitments I haven't thought through because the calendar says it's time. Marriage in particular takes money, time and emotional energy. Throwing a wedding is hardly the finish line. I can close a stock app when prices fall. Life doesn't have that button.

I still want to study quantitative trading. I don't assume traders can never be replaced. I want to understand a method I can test repeatedly and spend less time being pulled around by headlines. In practice, it's almost a comedy: I say I'll study while refreshing X, pick up a book, then find myself in the comments three minutes later. News, quotes and social media chop up my attention. At the end of the day I feel busy and struggle to name what I actually did.

After that conversation, the first thing I wanted to change was how I spend my attention. Put the phone farther away, take class seriously, keep training, and give AI and trading time. “Lean muscle, Sun studies, US stocks and AI” sounds like a formula for the moment. For me the first step is simply this: stop scrolling and finish today's work 😂.

数学题算错两次之后 我以前发推吐槽过：一个小小的分部积分，居然算错两次。那种感觉很熟悉——明明知道公式，写到纸上还是能把符号、上下限或者中间一步弄丢。 我以前发推吐槽过：一个小小的分部积分，居然算错两次。那种感觉很熟悉——明明知道公式，写到纸上还是能把符号、上下限或者中间一步弄丢。矩阵、行列式也一样，听别人讲的时候“嗯嗯我会了”，自己落笔又卡住。

后来我给自己换了个要求：先别急着要答案，把“这一步为什么能这么变”说出来。做电路题也是，电流从哪来，方向怎么定，公式和图上的元件是不是对得上。如果只能对着标准答案点头，我下一题大概率还会摔一跤。

这个栏目以后会放我真正做过、复核过的笔记。错题也会留着，毕竟它们比“我又学会了一个知识点”更诚实。

拿逆矩阵来说，知道公式和真的算对是两回事。我现在会先问矩阵是不是方阵、行列式是不是零；若可逆，再选伴随矩阵法或初等行变换。算完用原矩阵乘回去，看是不是单位矩阵。这个“乘回去”的动作特别重要，它比盯着答案猜自己对没对有用。

电路题也一样。我会把已知量、参考方向和所求量先写清楚，再列方程。算出负电流不等于做错，可能只是实际方向与假设相反。真正麻烦的是没设方向就开始代数，最后连自己在算哪条支路都说不清。把这些小地方讲明白，才算从“会看题解”往“会做题”挪了一步。
text_en:
Learning electrical engineering Circuits, control diagrams and mathematics need explanations, not just answers. I once complained on X that I got a little integration-by-parts problem wrong twice. I know the formula, yet a sign, a bound or a step still goes missing on paper. Matrices and determinants do the same thing to me. I nod along when someone explains them, then get stuck as soon as I pick up a pen.

I started asking myself to explain why each step is valid before looking for an answer. With circuit problems, I ask where the current comes from, how I chose its direction, and whether each equation matches the components in the diagram. If all I can do is nod at the worked solution, the next problem will probably trip me up again.

This section is for problems I've actually worked through and checked. I'll keep my mistakes, too. They're a more honest record than announcing I've learned another concept.

Take matrix inverses. Knowing a formula and getting the inverse right are different skills. I first ask if the matrix is square and whether its determinant is zero. If it is invertible, I choose between the adjugate and elementary row operations. Then I multiply by the original matrix to see if I get the identity. That last step tells me more than staring at the answer and guessing.

With circuits I write down the known quantities, reference directions and unknowns before setting up equations. A negative current can simply mean the actual direction is opposite to my assumption. The real trouble is starting the algebra without choosing directions and forgetting which branch I'm calculating. Explaining those small things is a step from reading a solution to solving the problem myself.

text_en:
Finding a study rhythm Study, exercise and rest are all part of the process. In one post I'd say, “Finish the run and drag yourself to the library,” and in the next I'd complain about my pace. Sometimes I'd study, open X, and then blame X for getting in the way. It's funny now, but at the time I wondered whether I even deserved a break if I hadn't finished the day's problems.

I don't want this section to be a discipline scoreboard. Study, exercise and sleep don't have to take points away from one another. When I feel good, I can do a little more. When I don't, I first try to work out why. I look at changes over time instead of judging myself on one day's pace or study hours.

I've talked about plenty of exercise and sleep data. I'll keep the numbers to myself. What I write here is about my experience and methods, rather than a training plan for someone else.

I used to cram driving lessons, tutoring, vocabulary, problem sets and exercise into one day. It looked great on paper and felt like sprinting for the last bus. Now I pick the one or two things that matter most and add more after they're done. A slow run is fine. At least I got outside.

I know social media steals my attention, and I still reach for it. Instead of vowing to quit my phone forever, I turn off notifications during study and give X a specific slot of its own. It's an ordinary method. Keeping it up for two weeks beats writing a perfect timetable.

text:
我从零折腾两台 VPS：买机器容易，养机器才是正片 最开始我对 VPS 的理解很朴素：买一台云服务器，装上系统，服务跑起来，手机能连，就算完成。真的折腾一圈才发现，“能连”是第一关，线路、维护、备份和账单，每一关都能让我重新打开 PowerShell。 最开始我对 VPS 的理解很朴素：买一台云服务器，装上系统，服务跑起来，手机能连，就算完成。真的折腾一圈才发现，“能连”是第一关，线路、维护、备份和账单，每一关都能让我重新打开 PowerShell。

**第一步：买的到底是什么。** 我在 Evoxt 买的是平台提供的虚拟机，不是先买一台物理服务器再自己装虚拟机。翻了一下订单，时间线是：2026 年 9 月 27 日先订购美国加州 VM-1，后来在 10 月 14 日订购马来西亚优质线路 VM-0.75。两笔都是按月付费，也都选了自动每周备份。官网下单时，流程是选地区和套餐、核对计费周期及可选项、完成支付，然后等订单确认、付款确认和“机器已部署”邮件。**订单邮件到了不等于机器已经能用**，我会等部署通知，再去控制台看状态。具体价格会随时间变化，文章不拿旧账单当报价表。

**第二步：拿到虚拟机，先别急着往里塞东西。** 控制台给出系统、地址和初始登录信息。我先确认虚拟机是 Running，再看系统版本、能否连接、磁盘和内存是否正常。美国那台最初收到的是 Ubuntu 24.04，后来有过重装和方案调整；马来西亚的部署通知显示 Ubuntu 26.04。重装会清掉系统盘上的旧配置，所以每次动手前得弄清什么要备份，什么可以丢。

**第三步：在 Windows 用 PowerShell 连上去。** 我不是在电脑里装了个“Linux 虚拟机”，而是从 Windows 终端远程登录云上的虚拟机。最基础的入口是 `ssh 用户名@服务器地址`。第一次连接要核对主机指纹；看到密码或密钥口令提示时，输入内容不会显示在屏幕上，这是正常的。连接成功后，我会先看系统信息、服务状态和网络，而不是一上来执行一大段来路不明的脚本。需要把文件从服务器取回本机，用的是 `scp`；需要核对下载文件是否一致，可以在 PowerShell 里用 `Get-FileHash`。下面把关键命令和排错顺序都列出来；真实地址和密钥当然不放在公开网页上。

**第四步：部署服务。** 早期试过不同方案，后来两台机器都围绕 sing-box 做过配置。实际操作并不是“复制教程，回车，完事”：要核对安装来源、检查配置格式、确认服务启动、设开机自启，再从手机端导入独立的连接信息进行测试。服务端显示 active，只能证明进程在跑；手机能不能连、实际应用顺不顺，必须另测。安装和服务管理的命令我对照了 sing-box 官方文档；具体协议字段随版本变化，实际配置时仍要以官方说明为准。

**第五步：手机实测，别只盯一个延迟数字。** 我测过马来西亚和美国节点，手机上看到的延迟大致是前者 100 多毫秒、后者 200 多毫秒。这个数字能说明当时的响应情况，不能直接等于下载速度，更不能代表晚高峰长期表现。后来我也比较过其他线路，发现服务器配置高不一定更快，跨境路由的影响很大。我的结论很朴素：先用真实场景测，再决定要不要继续花钱折腾。

**第六步：维护。** 服务能用以后还要看开机启动、系统更新、失败登录拦截、密钥登录、备份和到期提醒。这里尤其要老实：回头翻操作记录，有些安全加固当时确实还没做完，不能因为“手机连上了”就写成“服务器已经万无一失”。账单也是，收到续费提醒并不等于已付款。我会定期核对控制台、服务状态和实际连接；遇到超时先分清是机器停了、服务没起来，还是线路本身慢。PowerShell 只是操作台，真正有效的是每一步都有检查结果和回退办法。

我把过程整理成**脱敏流程**和**操作小抄**：`ssh` 负责连接，`scp` 负责传文件，`Get-FileHash` 核对文件；Linux 端的服务状态与日志命令负责确认服务是否正常。真实 IP、密码、二维码、连接参数、订单号和账单不会公开。这样别人能看懂我怎么走过来，也不会顺手拿到我家的钥匙。

**把部署这一步展开：从安装到手机填写。** 前面是我当时折腾两台机器的时间线。下面这份是按官方文档整理的通用复现示例，方便以后重装时对照；它没有在一台新机器上重新跑过，不能冒充另一份实测报告。真实配置里的 UUID、密钥和地址都换成了占位符。服务器按月付费，是我原来的个人开销；这个网站本身仍用免费的 GitHub Pages。

**1．先分清两个终端。** PowerShell 在 Windows 上；SSH 登录成功以后，提示符变了，后面的 Linux 命令才是在云服务器里运行。我以前最容易把这里混在一起。先在 PowerShell 里检查连接端口，再登录：

```powershell
$serverAddress = "替换为自己的服务器地址"
$sshPort = 22 # 如果自己改过 SSH 端口，这里也要改
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName $serverAddress -Port $sshPort
ssh -p $sshPort "root@$serverAddress"
```

`TcpTestSucceeded` 是 `True` 说明 TCP 端口能连，不等于 SSH 密码已经正确，更不等于后面的代理服务能用。第一次出现主机指纹，和控制台等可信渠道核对后再接受。服务器重装后指纹可能变化，也要核对，别看见提示就闭眼删记录。

**2．在 Ubuntu 安装官方软件包。** 先查看系统版本、更新软件索引，再装基础工具。这里的命令在 SSH 会话中运行，不是在本机 PowerShell 里运行：

```bash
cat /etc/os-release
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ca-certificates curl openssl nano
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl --fail --silent --show-error --location https://sing-box.app/gpg.key --output /etc/apt/keyrings/sagernet.asc
sudo chmod 0644 /etc/apt/keyrings/sagernet.asc
```

把下面的软件源内容写入文件。每一段执行后先看有没有报错，别让上一条失败了、下一条还在热闹地跑：

```bash
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/sagernet.sources > /dev/null <<'EOF'
Types: deb
URIs: https://deb.sagernet.org/
Suites: *
Components: *
Enabled: yes
Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/sagernet.asc
EOF
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install sing-box
sing-box version
```

安装来源与后续变更见 [官方包管理器安装说明](https://sing-box.sagernet.org/installation/package-manager/)。最后一条应显示实际版本；如果软件源、签名或网络报错，先处理报错，不改用不知道谁维护的一键包凑数。

**3．生成每台机器自己的凭证。** 下面三条分别生成 UUID、REALITY 密钥对和一个短标识。输出只放在自己的安全记录里：

```bash
cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid
sing-box generate reality-keypair
openssl rand -hex 4
```

密钥对里有私钥和公钥：私钥留服务器，手机用公钥。别看它们长得差不多就随便复制，填反了可不会因为我态度诚恳就连上。两台服务器各自生成一套，手机里也分别命名，省得以后排错时连自己到底在测哪台都不知道。

**4．写配置，再检查配置。** 我后来的方案围绕 VLESS／REALITY。下面给出一个字段对照示例：把 `YOUR_UUID`、`YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`、`YOUR_SHORT_ID` 和两处 `YOUR_HANDSHAKE_HOST` 替换成自己的值，保留引号。握手目标需要从服务器可达并符合 REALITY 的要求，不能随手填个域名当装饰。字段解释见 [VLESS 入站](https://sing-box.sagernet.org/configuration/inbound/vless/) 与 [REALITY TLS 配置](https://sing-box.sagernet.org/configuration/shared/tls/#reality-fields)。

```json
{
  "log": { "level": "warn", "timestamp": true },
  "inbounds": [{
    "type": "vless",
    "tag": "vless-in",
    "listen": "0.0.0.0",
    "listen_port": 443,
    "users": [{ "uuid": "YOUR_UUID", "flow": "xtls-rprx-vision" }],
    "tls": {
      "enabled": true,
      "server_name": "YOUR_HANDSHAKE_HOST",
      "reality": {
        "enabled": true,
        "handshake": { "server": "YOUR_HANDSHAKE_HOST", "server_port": 443 },
        "private_key": "YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY",
        "short_id": ["YOUR_SHORT_ID"]
      }
    }
  }],
  "outbounds": [{ "type": "direct", "tag": "direct" }],
  "route": { "final": "direct" }
}
```

用 `sudo nano /etc/sing-box/config.json` 打开配置文件，填好后保存。已有配置先备份，再编辑。然后检查：

```bash
sudo sing-box check -c /etc/sing-box/config.json
sudo systemctl cat sing-box
sudo ss -lntp
```

第一条检查语法和字段；第二条确认服务实际从哪里读配置；第三条看 443 有没有被别的程序占用。配置检查通过，也只是检查通过，还没到手机能用的那一步。如果服务读取的路径与示例不同，先统一路径。不要为了空出端口就把一个不认识的服务停掉。

**5．放行端口，启动服务。** 服务商控制台的入站规则要允许自己使用的服务端口。若系统本身启用了防火墙，还要检查系统规则；SSH 用哪个端口，就先确保哪个端口仍然放行，保留当前连接并用第二个窗口验证。示例的服务端口是 TCP 443，不需要把所有端口统统打开。

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now sing-box
sudo systemctl is-active sing-box
sudo systemctl is-enabled sing-box
sudo journalctl -u sing-box --output cat -e
```

这里分别看启动是否成功、是否正在运行、是否开机启动，以及具体日志。若是已经运行的服务，改配置后先通过检查，再执行 `sudo systemctl restart sing-box`。`active` 不是结束语，客户端连接仍然要单独验收。

**6．手机端各字段怎么对。** 在支持这个协议组合的客户端里新建配置，逐项对应；不同客户端叫法可能略有不同：

- 地址填服务器公网地址，端口填服务端的 `listen_port`。
- 协议选 VLESS，UUID 填刚生成的 UUID，flow 对应 `xtls-rprx-vision`。
- 开启 TLS，SNI／服务器名称填同一握手目标。
- REALITY 公钥填刚生成的公钥，short ID 填同一个短标识；私钥不进手机配置。
- 若客户端要求指纹，按其兼容说明填写；不要把“跳过证书校验”当成通用修复开关。

保存后先尝试连接，再打开实际网页或应用。连接日志报认证错误，就回头对 UUID、公钥、short ID 和 SNI；超时则先查地址、端口、入站规则和线路。我的手机当时测到马来西亚 100 多毫秒、美国 200 多毫秒，那是那一刻的延迟，不是套餐自带的永久承诺。

**7．维护不是再装一次。** 配置改动前留一份私密备份，记住当前版本；升级后重新检查配置并测试连接。异常时先看日志和端口，别把“重装系统”当万能橡皮擦。账单是否续上、控制台备份是否成功、备份能不能恢复，也都得真的点进去看。安全加固里还有没做完的项目，我会接着做，不能靠文章替机器毕业。
text_en:
VPS setup and maintenance A retrospective on deployment, phone tests and maintenance. At first my idea of a VPS was simple: buy a cloud server, install an operating system, start a service and connect from my phone. I found out that a working connection was just the first hurdle. Routing, maintenance, backups and bills all gave me reasons to open PowerShell again.

**What did I actually buy?** I rented virtual machines from Evoxt rather than buying hardware and setting up my own hypervisor. I ordered a California VM-1 on September 27, 2026 and a Malaysia premium-route VM-0.75 on October 14. Both were billed monthly, with automatic weekly backups selected. On the website I chose a region and plan, checked the billing cycle and extras, paid, and waited for order, payment and deployment emails. An order email doesn't say that a machine is ready. I wait for deployment and check the console. Prices change, so my old bills aren't a price list.

**The first checks on a new VM.** The console provides the OS, address and initial login information. I check that the VM is running, then check the OS version, connectivity, disk and memory. The US machine initially had Ubuntu 24.04 and later went through reinstalls and configuration changes. The Malaysia notice showed Ubuntu 26.04. Reinstalling wipes configurations on the system disk, so I work out what needs a backup before starting.

**Connecting with PowerShell on Windows.** I used a Windows terminal to log in remotely, not a VM installed on my PC. The basic command is `ssh username@server-address`. Check the host fingerprint on your first connection. Passwords and key passphrases don't appear as you type them. Once in, I check the system, services and network before running any script. I use `scp` to copy files back and `Get-FileHash` in PowerShell to check them. The commands below use placeholders instead of my address and keys.

**Deploying the service.** After trying different approaches, I configured sing-box on both machines. I checked the source of the package and the configuration format, verified the service started, set it to start at boot, then tested separate connection details on my phone. An active server process only tells me it's running. Actual mobile connectivity and application behavior need their own checks. I used the official documentation for setup and service commands. Protocol fields can change between versions.

**Testing on the phone.** I saw latency in the low hundreds of milliseconds for Malaysia and above 200 ms for the US. That was responsiveness at the time of the test, not a measure of download speed or long-run peak-hour performance. Comparing other routes taught me that higher server specs don't guarantee a better connection. Cross-border routes matter a great deal. I test my actual use case before spending more.

**Maintenance.** Once the service worked, I still had to look at boot startup, updates, repeated login failures, key-based login, backups and renewal reminders. Some hardening work was still open in my records. A connection on my phone doesn't say anything about whether it's done. A renewal notice doesn't mean the bill was paid. I check the console, service status and real connections regularly. On a timeout I first work out whether the VM is down, the service stopped, or the route is slow. PowerShell is my console. The useful part is having a result and a way back at each step.

I kept a redacted workflow and cheat sheet. SSH connects, SCP moves files, and Get-FileHash checks them. On Linux, service and log commands help me verify operation. My real IP addresses, passwords, QR codes, connection parameters, order numbers and bills stay private.

**From installation to entering the phone settings.** The timeline above is about my two machines. The example below comes from the official docs and is for reference on a future reinstall. I haven't rerun it on a fresh machine. UUIDs, keys and addresses here are placeholders. The servers are a personal monthly expense. The site itself is hosted on free GitHub Pages.

**1. Know which terminal you're in.** PowerShell runs on Windows. After SSH login, the prompt changes and subsequent Linux commands run on the server. I used to mix that up. First check the port in PowerShell, then log in.

```powershell
$serverAddress = "YOUR_SERVER_ADDRESS"
$sshPort = 22 # Change this if SSH uses a different port
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName $serverAddress -Port $sshPort
ssh -p $sshPort "root@$serverAddress"
```

When `TcpTestSucceeded` is `True`, the TCP port is reachable. It doesn't validate the SSH password or say the service will work. Compare the first host fingerprint with the provider console or another trusted source. Reinstalling can change it. Verify that change before removing the remembered fingerprint.

**2. Install the official package on Ubuntu.** Check the OS, update the package index and install the tools. Run these in the SSH session.

```bash
cat /etc/os-release
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ca-certificates curl openssl nano
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl --fail --silent --show-error --location https://sing-box.app/gpg.key --output /etc/apt/keyrings/sagernet.asc
sudo chmod 0644 /etc/apt/keyrings/sagernet.asc
```

Write the package source as shown below. Check each block for errors before moving on.

```bash
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/sagernet.sources > /dev/null <<'EOF'
Types: deb
URIs: https://deb.sagernet.org/
Suites: *
Components: *
Enabled: yes
Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/sagernet.asc
EOF
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install sing-box
sing-box version
```

See the [official package-manager instructions](https://sing-box.sagernet.org/installation/package-manager/) for sources and changes. The last command should show the installed version. If the repository, signature or network fails, investigate the error before using another distribution method.

**3. Generate separate credentials per machine.** These commands generate a UUID, a REALITY key pair and a short ID. Store the output securely.

```bash
cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid
sing-box generate reality-keypair
openssl rand -hex 4
```

Keep the private key on the server and enter the public key on the phone. Use a separate set for each machine and give the phone profiles distinct names so you know which one you're testing.

**4. Write and check the configuration.** My later setup used VLESS with REALITY. Replace `YOUR_UUID`, `YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`, `YOUR_SHORT_ID` and both copies of `YOUR_HANDSHAKE_HOST` with your own values, keeping the quotes. The handshake target must be reachable from the server and meet REALITY's requirements. See [VLESS inbound](https://sing-box.sagernet.org/configuration/inbound/vless/) and [REALITY TLS settings](https://sing-box.sagernet.org/configuration/shared/tls/#reality-fields).

```json
{
  "log": { "level": "warn", "timestamp": true },
  "inbounds": [{
    "type": "vless",
    "tag": "vless-in",
    "listen": "0.0.0.0",
    "listen_port": 443,
    "users": [{ "uuid": "YOUR_UUID", "flow": "xtls-rprx-vision" }],
    "tls": {
      "enabled": true,
      "server_name": "YOUR_HANDSHAKE_HOST",
      "reality": {
        "enabled": true,
        "handshake": { "server": "YOUR_HANDSHAKE_HOST", "server_port": 443 },
        "private_key": "YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY",
        "short_id": ["YOUR_SHORT_ID"]
      }
    }
  }],
  "outbounds": [{ "type": "direct", "tag": "direct" }],
  "route": { "final": "direct" }
}
```

I use `sudo nano /etc/sing-box/config.json` to edit the configuration after backing up the existing file. Then I check it.

```bash
sudo sing-box check -c /etc/sing-box/config.json
sudo systemctl cat sing-box
sudo ss -lntp
```

The first command checks syntax and fields. The second shows where the service reads its configuration. The third checks whether anything is already listening on port 443. If the service reads a different path, resolve that before proceeding. Identify a service before stopping it to free a port.

**5. Allow the port and start the service.** The provider's inbound rules must allow the service port. Check the OS firewall if it's enabled. Keep the SSH port allowed, leave the current session open and verify a second connection. This example needs TCP 443 for the service.

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now sing-box
sudo systemctl is-active sing-box
sudo systemctl is-enabled sing-box
sudo journalctl -u sing-box --output cat -e
```

These commands start the service and check if it's running, enabled at boot, and what the logs say. If it's already running, validate the updated configuration before running `sudo systemctl restart sing-box`. Verify the client separately.

**6. Match the phone fields.** In a client that supports this combination, create a profile. Field names can vary.

- Use the public server address and the server's `listen_port`.
- Select VLESS and enter the UUID you generated. Set the flow to `xtls-rprx-vision`.
- Enable TLS and use the same handshake host as the SNI or server name.
- Enter the REALITY public key and the matching short ID. Keep the private key on the server.
- If the client needs a fingerprint, follow its compatibility instructions. Skipping certificate verification isn't a general fix.

Save it, try connecting, then open a real page or app. For errors in the authentication log, verify the UUID, public key, short ID and SNI. For a timeout, check the address, port, inbound rules and route. The phone readings of over 100 ms for Malaysia and over 200 ms for the US were snapshots, rather than permanent attributes of the plans.

**7. Maintenance goes beyond reinstalling.** Make a private backup and record the current version before changing the configuration. Check it and test the connection again after an upgrade. Start with logs and listening ports when something goes wrong. Check whether renewals went through, console backups ran successfully and the backups actually restore. I still have hardening work to do.

我们抓过故障时的通信日志：读取请求不断出现，但没有成功完成的记录。普通的软件重置不是每次有效，电源复位曾让它恢复；触控板固件更新还出现过失败，Windows 显示“更新包安装成功”也不能说明固件已经刷进去。现在最有依据的是供电、固件或硬件链路相关的问题，但具体哪一处坏了，证据还不够。

Investigating a failing touchpad Logs and real input tests matter more than a status icon. My laptop's touchpad puts on a good show. The system sometimes says the device is working normally while the cursor won't move under my finger. Clicking and two-finger scrolling stop working too. I wanted a one-click fix, but the Device Manager status wasn't enough. I needed to look at actual input and lower-level logs.

We captured communication logs during a failure. Read requests kept appearing without successful completions. An ordinary software reset didn't always help, and a power reset brought it back once. A touchpad firmware update also failed. A Windows message that the update package installed doesn't prove the firmware flashed. The evidence points toward power, firmware or the hardware connection, but I can't yet say which one failed.

I set up automated monitoring and recovery attempts to record faults and save a manual step when recovery is possible. If the touchpad fails again, the logs give me somewhere to start. The BIOS and firmware checks I'm still working through belong on the open list.

最后清理的是能确认的东西，保留的是用途不明或内容不同的东西。受保护目录当时也没有被完整读到，所以我不会写“全盘都检查完了”。这件事听起来不刺激，但比“一键清理出几十 GB”靠谱：先比内容，再看占用，动手之后复查可用空间和还在用的项目。

我当时的顺序是先看哪些目录占空间，再区分缓存、安装包、备份和正在使用的项目。名字相同只是线索，不是删除凭据；重要文件还要比大小、路径、修改时间，必要时算哈希。确认重复之后再动手，动完看应用和项目还能不能正常打开。

这次还有个现实边界：当前会话没有管理员权限，受保护目录的完整读取没有做成。这个结果不影响已经核对的缓存清理，但也不能被写成“C 盘彻底体检完成”。以后再清理，我会先保留一份删除清单和空间变化，省得靠记忆解释自己删过什么。

Maintaining a Windows PC Verify duplicates, make reversible changes and keep unresolved issues visible. When I cleared space on my C drive, I worried about missing things I could delete and deleting things I needed. The scan turned up caches, old installer files and verified duplicates. A few research projects looked like copies but contained results unique to each, so I couldn't just wipe them together to save time.

I cleared what I could verify and kept anything with a different purpose or contents I couldn't account for. Some protected folders weren't fully accessible. The practical sequence was to compare contents, check space usage, and then review free space and the projects I still needed after cleanup.

I started by finding the biggest folders and distinguishing caches, installers, backups and active projects. Matching names are a lead. For important files I also compare size, paths and modification times, and compute hashes where useful. I check that apps and projects still open after removing confirmed duplicates.

The session didn't have administrator rights, so I couldn't fully inspect protected directories. That didn't affect the cache cleanup I could verify. Next time I want to keep a deletion list and record the space reclaimed so I don't have to reconstruct it from memory.

AI 对我最有用的地方：把想法真的做出来 我当然喜欢问 AI 问题，但最上头的不是它说得多漂亮，而是我说“想做个网站”，最后真有网址能打开；说“做个平行宇宙报社”，最后真有一期能搜、能收藏的报纸。 我当然喜欢问 AI 问题，但最上头的不是它说得多漂亮，而是我说“想做个网站”，最后真有网址能打开；说“做个平行宇宙报社”，最后真有一期能搜、能收藏的报纸。过程里它也会说错、会把没验证的东西讲得像已经完成，这时候就得把它拽回现实：链接呢？文件呢？手机打开了吗？

我给自己定的规矩是，项目至少过三关：东西做出来、关键功能自己试过、别人能在真实设备上用。AI 是一起干活的工具，不是替我宣布胜利的主持人。这个栏目会写实际使用过程和失败记录，不发“十个神仙提示词”那种看完就忘的清单。

我通常先说清楚想要的成品是什么，再把已有材料和不能乱碰的地方列出来。做网站时，成品是能打开的页面；做报社时，成品不只是几篇新闻，还包括搜索、收藏和离线阅读。任务一拆开，AI 才不会把“我给你想了个好点子”当成交差。

另一关是核对。比如网站国内能不能直连，我自己手机的一次成功只能说明那一次；要说电信、联通、移动都行，就得真用大陆节点测。再比如一封续费提醒，看到邮件不等于账单已付。AI 如果把推测说成结果，我就回头找页面、日志、邮件和实测记录。这样折腾很啰嗦，但比“看起来做完了”强。
text_en:
Working with AI on real projects Define the goal, make a reviewable result and test it in the real world. I like asking AI questions, but what hooks me is saying “I want to build a website” and ending up with a link I can open. Or asking for a parallel-universe newspaper and getting an issue I can search and save. AI can get things wrong and describe an untested result as done. That's when I bring it back to the real thing: Where's the link? Where's the file? Did it open on my phone?

My projects go through three stages. Make the thing, try the main functions myself, and let someone use it on a real device. AI works alongside me. This section is about what happened in practice, including the failures, rather than a list of supposedly magical prompts.

I usually describe what a finished result looks like, then list the existing material and what needs to be preserved. For the site, the result is a page that opens. For the newspaper, it's articles plus search, favorites and offline reading. Breaking the work down helps keep a clever idea from being mistaken for a delivered project.

Then I verify it. One successful connection on my phone in China only describes that attempt. A claim about China Telecom, China Unicom and China Mobile needs real mainland test nodes. Seeing a renewal email doesn't tell me a bill was paid. When AI turns a guess into a result, I go back to the page, logs, email or test record. It's tedious and gives me something I can check.

text:
我的网站为什么改了又改 最早我把网站分成七个栏目，却忘了栏目里还没有真实文章。手机打开时，两个卡片光秃秃地站在那儿，底部进度条还没走完，我第一反应是：完了，国内网是不是又卡了？ 最早我把网站分成七个栏目，却忘了栏目里还没有真实文章。手机打开时，两个卡片光秃秃地站在那儿，底部进度条还没走完，我第一反应是：完了，国内网是不是又卡了？检查后才发现，页面主体其实已经出来了，空白主要是内容和固定高度的组合问题。

后来我参考一个喜欢的小站，把配色改成深色，卡片压紧，留白给标题和正文。GitHub Pages 还是免费托管；我自己用手机关掉代理试过一次，能直连。至于不同省份、不同运营商是不是都稳，没有大陆节点的持续测试就不装懂。这个网站会继续改，但每次改完，我都要拿手机看一眼，不能只在电脑上自我感觉良好。

第一次上线，我先把页面框架、栏目和基础交互放上去，再用 GitHub Pages 免费发布。它的好处是不用为一个个人站每月交托管费；代价是线路体验不一定稳定，尤其手机网络和电脑网络走的路径未必一样。那张手机截图后来给我上了一课：看到“加载了一半”，先分清页面结构、资源请求和内容本身哪个出了问题。

这轮改版，我把文章写成独立页面，栏目封面直接对应内容，手机读长文不用挤在弹窗里。七个栏目都挂上实际文章，首页摘要也检查到句号再收尾。发布以后还要逐一打开文章、图片和联系邮箱，不能只看首页亮了就庆祝。
text_en:
Building this website Free hosting, content structure, mobile layout and a direct phone test. At first I divided the site into seven sections and forgot that some didn't have real articles yet. On my phone, two bare cards stood there while the progress bar was still moving. My first thought was that the connection in China had stalled again. The main page had already loaded. The blank space mostly came from empty content combined with fixed heights.

I took inspiration from a site I liked, switched to a dark palette, tightened the cards, and left more breathing room for titles and text. GitHub Pages still hosted it for free. I turned off my proxy and connected directly once on my phone. I would need ongoing mainland tests to say how it behaves across provinces and carriers. I'll keep changing the site, and I want to look at it on a phone after each change.

On the first release I put together the page structure, sections and basic interactions, then published it on GitHub Pages. I didn't have to pay monthly hosting for a personal site. The tradeoff is that network conditions vary, and mobile and desktop connections may take different routes. That phone screenshot taught me to figure out which part looks half-loaded: the page structure, a resource request, or the content itself.

I moved articles to their own pages, matched covers with the sections, and made long notes easier to read on a phone without squeezing them into a pop-up. All seven sections got real articles, and I checked that homepage summaries ended at full sentences. After publishing, I still need to open the articles and images and check the contact address. A lit-up homepage is only the first check.

text:
每日简报：别把“看到提醒”写成“事情解决了” 我做过新闻与商业信息的简报，也做过只读检查日历和收件箱的个人简报。做多了才发现，最容易出错的不是漏掉一条新闻，而是把状态说满：收到续费邮件，不代表已经扣款；日历查不到，不代表今天一定没安排；某个邮箱连不上，就得老实写“没查到”。 我做过新闻与商业信息的简报，也做过只读检查日历和收件箱的个人简报。做多了才发现，最容易出错的不是漏掉一条新闻，而是把状态说满：收到续费邮件，不代表已经扣款；日历查不到，不代表今天一定没安排；某个邮箱连不上，就得老实写“没查到”。

我希望简报帮我少忘事，而不是制造一种“所有事情都被 AI 管好了”的幻觉。来源、时间、我需要做什么，这三样比花哨排版更重要。私人邮件和账单不会搬到网站上，网站只讲这套核对方法。

我把个人简报和新闻简报分开看。前者负责提醒我今天可能要处理什么：日历安排、未读邮件、付款期限、需要回复的人；后者负责把新闻和商业信息整理成可以快速浏览的线索。两者都要写清时间和来源，但不能互相替代。新闻写得再热闹，也不能替我确认自己的账单有没有扣款。

如果某个邮箱临时连不上，我宁愿把“本次没核对到”写在显眼处；如果邮件只说“即将到期”，就保留这个状态，不替服务商宣布扣款成功。最重要的一步其实发生在简报之后：我再去点开原始邮件、日历或账户，把真要处理的事做掉。简报是路标，不是替我办事的手。
text_en:
A careful briefing workflow Check sources and dates, and keep unresolved items unresolved. I've made news and business briefings as well as personal ones based on read-only checks of my calendar and inbox. The easiest mistake is overstating a status. A renewal email doesn't show that a payment went through. An empty calendar result doesn't guarantee an empty day. If I can't reach an inbox, I need to say so.

I want a briefing to help me forget fewer things. Sources, times and actions matter more than fancy formatting. Private emails and invoices stay private. The method is what belongs on this site.

I treat the two kinds of briefing separately. A personal one tells me what might need attention today: an appointment, unread email, payment deadline or person to reply to. A news briefing organizes stories and business information so I can skim for leads. Both need sources and dates. An engaging news item won't tell me whether my own bill was paid.

If an inbox is unavailable, I make “couldn't check this time” easy to see. If the email says a bill is coming due, I leave it at that. The most important step comes afterward, when I open the original email, calendar entry or account and take care of the actual task. The briefing points me toward it.

text:
平行宇宙报社：给不存在的世界排一期报 起点是一个很好玩的设问：如果 AI 给一个不存在的世界写新闻，会发生什么？后来它变成了“平行宇宙报社”的《25 小时世界》一期。 起点是一个很好玩的设问：如果 AI 给一个不存在的世界写新闻，会发生什么？后来它变成了“平行宇宙报社”的《25 小时世界》一期。光有奇怪设定不够，我还想让它看起来真的像一份报纸：标题、栏目、搜索、收藏和离线阅读都得能用。

最难的不是写一句“这个世界一天有 25 小时”，而是让每条新闻都遵守这个世界的规则。写着写着如果自己先忘了设定，读者一定更出戏。这个项目已经上线过，原站也保留下来了。跨地区访问是否稳定，当时没有足够的国内节点实测，所以我把它当作创作和产品实验，不把网络问题一笔带过。

我给这个项目定过几个很实际的要求：读者要能按主题找内容，看到喜欢的能收藏，断网之后也还能读到已经保存的部分。做起来才发现，创意站也逃不开那些“小事”：标题怎么摆，搜索有没有结果，刷新后收藏还在不在，手机上会不会挤成一团。世界观负责让人想点开，细节负责让人愿意继续逛。

我很喜欢这种玩法，因为它让我把“写故事”和“做产品”放在同一个桌面上。一个点子如果只存在于聊天框里，很容易觉得自己已经做了很多；真正变成网页，问题才会一个个冒出来。对我来说，这些冒出来的问题就是项目最值钱的部分。
text_en:
Parallel Universe Press A fictional newspaper with search, favorites and offline reading. The project began with a fun question: what would happen if AI wrote news for a world that doesn't exist? It became the “25-Hour World” issue of Parallel Universe Press. The odd premise was only the start. I wanted a paper with headlines and sections, working search, favorites, and offline reading.

The hard part was getting every story to obey the rules of a 25-hour world. If I forgot the setting as I wrote, the reader would notice. The project went live and I kept the original site. I didn't have enough mainland test nodes to assess how steadily it could be reached across regions. I treat it as a creative and product experiment and keep that question open.

I set practical requirements: find stories by topic, save favorites, and read previously saved material offline. Creative sites still have all the little details, from headline placement and useful search results to surviving a refresh with favorites intact and fitting on a phone. The world gets someone to open the paper. The details help them keep reading.

I like the project because writing a story and building a product happen at the same desk. An idea in a chat window can feel farther along than it is. Making it a real webpage brings the problems out one by one. Those are the parts of the project I value most.

text:
追夜：五座城市亮灯之后 我做过一支五座城市夜景的视频，从画面、双语字幕到封面、标题和平台发布文案，前后改了好几版。真正准备发布时，我选择自己来按上传按钮，资料则提前整理好。 我做过一支五座城市夜景的视频，从画面、双语字幕到封面、标题和平台发布文案，前后改了好几版。真正准备发布时，我选择自己来按上传按钮，资料则提前整理好。做视频的乐趣当然是画面，但后来我更能理解：字幕、素材来源、版权检查、封面和文件版本，都决定一支片子能不能稳稳落地。

再后来，我让电脑把这个视频项目的成片、素材、缓存和备份都清掉了。不是“还藏着一个下载链接”，就是删了。因此这里写的是这次制作的过程，不放一个已经不存在的作品入口。平行宇宙报社则按我的要求保留了，这两个项目不能混为一谈。

一条视频从想法到能上传，中间其实有不少容易漏掉的环节。画面顺序要能讲清故事，字幕得能读，封面要让人一眼知道主题，发布文案得和成片对应。双语字幕尤其容易出现“中文还行，英文一眼机翻”的尴尬，我只能一遍遍看实际画面，不能光看文字稿。

后来清理文件是我自己决定的，不是什么“创作中断”的戏剧故事。电脑空间要留给下一件事，已经结束的项目也没必要永远堆着。留下一篇过程记录，反而比留十份命名混乱的备份更能帮我回想当时是怎么做的。
text_en:
After Dark: a five-city video experiment A bilingual night-city video and a complete publishing package. I made a night video set in five cities and went through several versions of the footage, bilingual subtitles, cover, title and platform descriptions. When it was ready, I chose to press Upload myself and got the publishing materials ready ahead of time. I enjoyed working on the pictures, but subtitles, sourcing, rights checks, covers and file versions all matter if I want to get a film out the door.

Later I had the computer delete the final video, source clips, caches and backups. There isn't a hidden download link. This page keeps a record of how I made it. I chose to keep Parallel Universe Press, which was a separate project.

Between a video idea and a file ready to upload there are plenty of steps to miss. The shot order needs to tell the story, the subtitles need to be readable, and the cover and description should match what's in the video. With bilingual subtitles it's easy for one language to look natural while the other reads like machine translation. I had to watch the footage repeatedly with the subtitles in place.

The cleanup was my choice, without a dramatic story about giving up on the project. I needed disk space for the next thing. One process note helps me remember what I did better than ten backups with confusing names.

text:
看电影、听歌，顺手记一点感受 我会因为电影的结局觉得遗憾，也会因为一段钢琴或者 City Pop 觉得脑子终于安静下来。公开推文和聊天里谈过电影、小说、流行音乐，但我不打算把每次“好听死了”硬扩写成一篇权威乐评。 我会因为电影的结局觉得遗憾，也会因为一段钢琴或者 City Pop 觉得脑子终于安静下来。公开推文和聊天里谈过电影、小说、流行音乐，但我不打算把每次“好听死了”硬扩写成一篇权威乐评。

这个栏目留给具体的感受：哪一幕让我停住，哪一段旋律让我反复听，后来想法有没有变。等我真写出完整影评或乐评，再把它们一篇篇挂上来。现在先把入口搭好，不拿 AI 编的观后感充数。

有时一段音乐好听，我第一反应就是再听一遍，而不是马上查曲风、写分析；一部电影看完难受，我也会先让那个情绪待一会儿。把感受记下来不是为了显得多懂，只是怕过两周连自己为什么喜欢都忘了。

我想把这个栏目当成私人票根：记当时的场景、让我停住的细节，以及过段时间再回头看有没有变。能查到作品信息就写清楚，记不准的情节不硬编。说不定以后翻到某篇，只会想起“那天风挺大，歌放得刚好”，这也够了。
text_en:
Reading, film and music Small reactions can become more thoughtful criticism. A movie ending can leave me with regret. Piano or City Pop can finally quiet my head. I've talked about films, novels and pop music in public posts and chats, but I don't have to make every “this sounds amazing” into authoritative criticism.

This section is for specific reactions: the scene that stopped me, the melody I kept replaying, and whether my feelings changed later. Full reviews can go here when I've actually written them. I can make room for them without filling it with opinions made up by AI.

Sometimes, when a piece of music sounds good, I'd rather play it again before looking up the genre or writing an analysis. When a film leaves me feeling awful, I let the feeling sit for a bit. I write it down because in two weeks I might forget why I liked it.

I think of this section as a stack of ticket stubs. I can keep the setting, the detail that caught me, and what it feels like to return to it later. I'll check credits or titles when I can and leave uncertain plot details out. Maybe one day an entry will remind me only that it was windy and the song came on at exactly the right moment. That's enough.

text:
三块屏幕和一张跑步路线 我的日常经常在电脑、手机和平板之间切。电脑上做网站，手机上试能不能打开；服务器在云上，PowerShell 在本机，真正的体验却得看手机。 我的日常经常在电脑、手机和平板之间切。电脑上做网站，手机上试能不能打开；服务器在云上，PowerShell 在本机，真正的体验却得看手机。设备一多，就很容易出现“电脑上没问题，手机怎么又不对了”的经典场面。

屏幕之外我也跑步、听歌、看天。推文里那些彩虹、夜空、回家路上的疲惫，比精心剪辑的“充实一天”更像真实生活。这个栏目以后可以慢慢放游记；眼下能核对的完整旅行素材不够，我不会凭空写一趟不存在的旅行。

跑步的时候我不怎么像那些运动博主：会嫌自己慢，会想偷懒，偶尔跑完还惦记回去刷手机。不过换个地方走走、抬头看一眼天空，脑子确实会从屏幕里退出来一点。夜色、彩虹、路边的猫，这些小东西在推文里出现过很多次。

生活碎片放在网站上，不用每篇都承担“给别人提供价值”的任务。有时只是留个证据：我那天出门了，看到了一点好看的东西，后来又回到书桌前。旅行写作等真有素材再做；现在这篇就写我确实过过的普通日子。
text_en:
Across phone, tablet and PC Everyday cross-device use is part of the garden. I switch between a computer, phone and tablet all day. I build the website on the computer and see if it opens on my phone. The server is in the cloud and PowerShell is on my PC, but the phone tells me what the experience is like. The more devices there are, the more often I hear myself say, “It worked on the computer. What happened here?”

Away from screens, I run, listen to music and look at the sky. The rainbows, night skies and tired journeys home in my posts feel closer to everyday life than a carefully edited “productive day.” This section can hold travel writing when I have enough material to check. So far I don't.

I don't run like an exercise influencer. I complain that I'm slow, want to skip it, and sometimes finish already thinking about checking my phone. But going somewhere different and looking up really does pull my attention out of the screen for a while. The night sky, rainbows and roadside cats keep showing up in my posts.

Little moments on a personal site don't all need to teach someone something. Sometimes they're just evidence that I went outside, saw something nice, then came back to my desk. Travel writing can wait until I have something to write about. These are the ordinary days I actually lived.

text:
F1 这么会赚钱，赛车本身还在 C 位吗？ 赛车负责跑圈，围场外的人负责跑流量。看了这么多年 F1，我越来越好奇，这个越来越大的生意，到底是谁在为谁买单？ 新加坡站结束后，我又想起今年看上海站时就在琢磨的一件事：F1 现在这么火，到底是谁在为谁买单？

我看了很多年 F1，比赛当然还得看，赛车一圈之内能发生的事，比不少电视剧一季的剧情都密。但镜头往围场外面一转，又是另一套节目：明星、名流、品牌酒会、高价内场票，像一场跟着赛车环球旅行的大型社交活动。新加坡站的 K-pop 明星，上海站的各路艺人，都自带一整套话题和粉丝。说白了，赛车负责跑圈，大家负责把热搜也跑起来。

我不知道每个到场的人究竟懂多少赛车，也没兴趣挨个出道试卷。只是作为车迷，看到最贵、最显眼的位置有时更像社交场，会有点别扭。但换个角度，主办方要的未必是人人都能聊轮胎策略：粉丝先因为偶像点进来，买票、看直播、买周边，F1 就又多了一条把人拉进来的路。以后真喜欢上比赛最好；就算只是来凑个热闹，流量也已经开始变现了。

赛车这个吞金兽，总得有人养。动力单元、底盘研发、车队运营、设备跨洲运输，哪样都不便宜。办赛费、转播版权、门票、赞助和周边，凑在一起才撑得起这个全球转的盘子。我原先想得比较狠：是不是小圈子的玩法撑不住了，才需要大众进来接盘？现在回头看，这话有点一刀切，但我的核心感觉没变——F1 越来越擅长把一场比赛做成一个全球娱乐生意，让更多人愿意为不同的东西掏钱。

奥迪和凯迪拉克也已经进入 2026 赛季的车队名单。我自己的看法是，除了赛道本身，它们一定也看中这个舞台的曝光和品牌想象力：让车迷记住名字，让潜在买家重新多看一眼。至于能带动多少销量，得拿结果说话，不能我坐这儿一拍脑袋就替财报填数。这里也附上 [FIA 2026 车队资料](https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/media_guide_2026_english.pdf)，免得把车迷聊天写成年份错乱的围场传闻。

我还想起同在上海赛车场的 China GT 赛车起火事件，以及当时看到的现场人员报酬讨论。网上流传过“60 元”这个数字，但我没找到足够的一手材料，这里先不把它当成已核实的工资单。真正让我在意的是另一件事：赛事看起来越来越像大生意，台后做救援、守安全的人，有没有分到与责任相称的训练、装备和待遇？

我不觉得“盘子小”就能替安全投入不足开脱。钱再紧，真到赛车起火的时候，冲上去的人也不能靠情怀灭火。明星、赞助商和贵宾区可以把比赛照得很亮，安全员可不是画面边角的摆设。前面赚曝光，后面省得抠抠搜搜，这账怎么看都不太顺眼。

说到底，流量确实能养活 F1，我也不指望它退回一个只有小圈子自娱自乐的年代。新车迷多了是好事，车队有资源做出好比赛也是好事。我只是希望，流量把舞台越撑越大的时候，赛车还在中间，真正把这场比赛托住的人也别被挤到边上去。别到最后热闹看了一整天，最不重要的反而成了比赛本身🤔。

As F1 makes more money, is racing still center stage? What fans, brands and hosts pay for, and what that business owes the people who keep racing safe. After the Singapore Grand Prix, I went back to a question I'd been thinking about since watching the Shanghai race earlier this year: now that F1 is this popular, who's paying for what?

I've watched F1 for years, and of course I still watch for the racing. A single lap can have more plot than a season of television. Pan the camera outside the paddock and there's another show: celebrities, socialites, brand parties and expensive hospitality tickets. It feels like a giant social event travelling around the world with the cars. The K-pop stars in Singapore and entertainers in Shanghai show up with their own stories and fans. The cars do laps, and everyone else gets the trending topics going.

I don't know how much each guest knows about racing, and I'm not going to hand out quizzes. As a fan, it can feel odd when the most expensive, visible spots look like a social scene. From an organizer's point of view, though, visitors don't all have to discuss tire strategy. Someone comes for their favorite star, buys a ticket, watches a broadcast or buys merchandise, and F1 has another way to bring people in. It's great if they discover the racing, but the attention is already generating revenue either way.

Someone has to feed this expensive machine. Power units, chassis development, team operations and moving equipment between continents all cost money. Hosting fees, broadcast rights, tickets, sponsorship and merchandise keep the global operation going. I used to wonder if a niche audience could no longer pay for it and the broader public had to pick up the bill. That was too sweeping, but my central impression holds: F1 is increasingly good at making a race into a global entertainment business that gives more people different things to spend on.

Audi and Cadillac are both on the 2026 team list. My view is that besides the racing, they see what this platform can do for visibility and how people perceive their brands. Fans remember the names and potential buyers may give them another look. Actual sales figures have to come from the results. I can't fill in a company's accounts from my sofa. Here's the [FIA 2026 team guide](https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/media_guide_2026_english.pdf) so the dates don't drift into paddock rumor.

I also thought of the China GT race-car fire at the same Shanghai circuit, and the discussions I saw about what track staff were paid. A figure of 60 yuan circulated online. I didn't find enough first-hand evidence to treat it as verified pay. What I care about is whether the people who respond to emergencies and keep everyone safe get training, equipment and compensation that match their responsibilities as the business grows.

A smaller event is no excuse to skimp on safety. When a car catches fire, the people running toward it can't put it out with enthusiasm alone. Stars, sponsors and hospitality suites help light up the show, but safety staff aren't scenery at the edge of the frame. Profiting from the exposure while pinching pennies backstage doesn't sit right with me.

Attention can help sustain F1. I don't expect it to go back to being a pastime for a small circle. More fans are welcome, and resources help teams put on good races. I hope the cars stay in the middle of the stage as it grows, and that the people who keep the race going have a place there too. It would be a shame to spend the whole day on the spectacle and find the race itself mattered least 🤔.
